source_reading.retention_owner: src/uar/runtime/manager.rs:1404 spawn_retention_sweeper wakes on session activity; the persisted TTL sweep (manager.rs:1660-1697) is opt-in through sessions.persisted_ttl_secs and deletes every session whose last_activity predates the cutoff (surreal.rs:2204 reads sessions.last_activity)

why_the_current_owned_instance_cannot_be: Its store is not empty: built-in seeding once cannot be observed.
Enabling persisted_ttl_secs there would let the real sweeper delete every older session in that store, including all prior scenario and operator data.
Embedded surrealkv is locked by the running process, so no host fixture can age one session's last_activity while UAR runs, which the contract requires.
provisioning_needed: A second disposable UAR instance on its own loopback port with a fresh store served by a local surreal server (surreal 3.2.0 is installed at /usr/local/bin/surreal), so a host fixture can update one captured session's last_activity
Config for that instance: sessions.persisted_ttl_secs set (for example 3600) and the same model provider configuration as the owned instance
Owner context for its session APIs from a second uar-jwt-proxy listener pointed at that instance (external infrastructure; the test sends no credentials)
next: Operator approval to provision the disposable instance, its surreal server and a second proxy listener; otherwise C52 stays BLOCKED.
